Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair

chip noun

a small piece broken or cut off

also chips, splinter, wood chip, shaving

classical

Plaut. Merc. 1.2.20 (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 16.54: assula tenuis brevisque (Lewis & Short)

assula, assulae f.

noun, first declension

chip, splinter

A chip or splinter of wood, and of marble (Vitr.). Potato chips are crisps or French fries (see those); a computer chip has no record here.

Other words

  • fragmentum, fragmentī n. — a piece broken off

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 34.39.11: tēgulārum (Lewis & Short)

    Any piece broken off, of tiles, bread or glass; mostly plural.

Examples

  • at etiam cessō foribus facere hīsce assulās

    and here I am, still holding back from smashing this door to splintersPlaut. Merc. 1.2.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • Faber lignārius asciat asciā māteriam, unde cadunt assulae

    The carpenter hews the timber with the adze, and chips fall from itComen. OP 63

See also piece, crumb, hew, crisps, French fries.

SourcesLewis & Short: assula · Lewis & Short: fragmentum
